## Description

Four changes to how Cosmos3 obtains its guardrail (verified on GPU nodes), plus CPU-only unit tests for the two new code paths.

### Bump `cosmos_guardrail` `0.3.0` → `0.3.1`

The version users are told to install (README + the `ImportError` hint in `pipeline_cosmos3.py`) moves to the `0.3.1` hotfix. Diffed the two wheels: bugfix-only, no API change, `Requires-Dist` identical — nothing in the TRT-LLM dependency set shifts. Everything the pipeline touches (`CosmosSafetyChecker`, `check_text_safety`, `check_video_safety`, `.text_guardrail`, `.video_guardrail`) is byte-identical. Fixes in 0.3.1: `allow_patterns` for `blocklist` / `video_content_safety_filter` were missing a trailing `/*` and matched nothing; blobs dir whitelisted in `nltk.data.path` for nltk ≥ 3.10; one spurious warning removed.

### Make the documented guardrail install actually importable

`cosmos_guardrail` imports `cv2` at module load and depends on the full `opencv-python` build. The README (and the matching `ImportError` hint in `pipeline_cosmos3.py`) told users to uninstall that build — correct, it is not allowed in TensorRT-LLM environments — but put nothing back, so `import cosmos_guardrail` failed with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'cv2'` and the pipeline refused to start. TensorRT-LLM itself carries no opencv by design; the example is the right place to install one. The instruction now adds `opencv-python-headless` after the uninstall, in that order so the headless build owns a complete `cv2/` directory.

Four changes to how Cosmos3 obtains its guardrail (verified on GPU nodes), plus CPU-only unit tests for the two new code paths.

### Fetch only the guardrail files that are actually loaded

`download_guardrail_checkpoint()` called `snapshot_download()` with no `allow_patterns`, pulling the whole `nvidia/Cosmos-1.0-Guardrail` repo — **17 GB** measured in the HF cache — of which `CosmosSafetyChecker` instantiates **135 MB**:

| subtree | size | loaded in 0.3.x |
|---|---|---|
| `aegis/` (LlamaGuard-7b + Aegis adapter) | 13 GB | no — no reference left in the package; Qwen3Guard replaced it |
| `video_content_safety_filter/` (SigLIP-so400m) | 3.3 GB | no — `VideoContentSafetyFilter` is commented out upstream |
| `face_blur_filter/Resnet50_Final.pth` | 110 MB | yes — `RetinaFaceFilter` |
| `blocklist/` | 26 MB | yes — `Blocklist` |

The fetch is now masked to `["blocklist/*", "face_blur_filter/*"]`. The mask is deliberately coupled to what the package loads (commented in `guardrails.py`): the library's own `snapshot_download` passes no revision, so anything our pinned pre-fetch misses would come off unpinned `main` rather than `GUARDRAIL_REVISION`. Widen it if a future `cosmos_guardrail` loads more.

Not changed: the checkpoint revision pin (`cf03c03`) is already the tip of that repo's `main`.

### Make the blocklist readable on nltk ≥ 3.10.3

The HF cache exposes every file in a snapshot as a symlink into `blobs/`, and `cosmos_guardrail`'s `Blocklist` points `nltk.data.path` at `<snapshot>/blocklist/nltk_data`. nltk 3.10.3 (2026-08-12) added `pathsec`, which opens data files with `O_NOFOLLOW` and raises `PermissionError` on a symlinked final component — with no opt-out (its docstring assumes "corpora/data files are never symlinks"). 0.3.1's own nltk fix whitelists `blobs/` in `nltk.data.path`, which satisfies the path-validation layer but not the open-time check. So on a **freshly populated cache**, `check_text_safety()` raises; caches populated by older huggingface_hub hold regular files and keep working, which is why existing installs don't see it.

`download_guardrail_checkpoint()` now copies each blob over its symlink under `blocklist/nltk_data` (temp file in the same directory + `os.replace`, so a crash leaves the symlink intact). That is the layout huggingface_hub produces with `HF_HUB_DISABLE_SYMLINKS=1`, limited to the ~25 MB nltk reads. The library's later `snapshot_download` leaves the copies alone — `_hf_hub_download_to_cache_dir` returns early on `os.path.exists(pointer_path)` without checking link-ness. Runs on both the cache-hit and download branches.

## Test Coverage

On 1×B200 with a native build of this branch, against an **empty** `HF_HOME` (the byte count is only meaningful on a cold cache):

```
mask     : ['blocklist/*', 'face_blur_filter/*']
--- after the masked download ---       TOTAL 135.3 MB
--- after CosmosSafetyChecker() ---     TOTAL 135.3 MB
library pulled an extra 0.0 MB from this repo
loaded models: ['Blocklist', 'Qwen3Guard', 'RetinaFaceFilter']
check_text_safety(benign) -> True
check_video_safety(blank) -> (4, 64, 64, 3)
```

The zero-growth line is the load-bearing one: constructing the checker after the masked download fetches nothing further, so the mask is complete, not merely smaller.

Unit tests — `test_cosmos3_pipeline.py`, `test_cosmos3_edge.py`, `test_cosmos3_distilled.py`, `test_cosmos3_transformer.py`, `test_offloading.py`: **329 passed, 0 failed** (54 deselected as integration). Note these cover the wiring only — `conftest.py::disable_cosmos3_guardrails` turns guardrails off suite-wide and the guardrail-path tests use fakes — which is why the real 0.3.1 package was exercised by hand above.

**nltk materialization** — 1×A10, nltk 3.10.3, `HF_HUB_DISABLE_SYMLINKS` unset, empty `HF_HOME`, both the download and cache-hit branches:

```
Materialized 75 nltk_data symlinks
nltk_data: 75 files, 0 symlinks, 0 leftover tmp, 0 hardlinked
face_blur_filter symlinks left untouched: 1
after CosmosSafetyChecker(): 75 files, 0 symlinks, 0 inodes changed
Blocklist.is_safe(benign)  -> True
Blocklist.is_safe(plurals) -> False 'Prompt blocked by censorship: … two **** carrying **** …'
[fresh] PASS   [prewarmed] PASS
```

The plurals line is the load-bearing one: "zombies"/"rifles" are not in the word lists, "zombie"/"rifle" are, so the block can only come from the `word_tokenize` + `WordNetLemmatizer` pass reading the materialized `nltk_data` — the exact path that raised before.

**Unit tests** — `tests/unittest/_torch/visual_gen/test_cosmos3_guardrails.py`, `cpu_only`, registered in `l0_cpu.yml`. No network, no checkpoint: `snapshot_download` is replaced by a recorder and the symlink handling runs against a synthetic HF-cache-shaped tree under `tmp_path`. Covers: both `snapshot_download` calls carry `repo_id`/`revision`/`allow_patterns` (dropping the mask on either path restores the 17 GB fetch); cache hit = exactly one `local_files_only` call; `GatedRepoError` → `ValueError`; materialization handles relative and absolute symlinks, produces regular files with `st_nlink == 1`, leaves `blocklist/custom/` and `face_blur_filter/` symlinks and the blobs untouched, leaves no temp files, is idempotent, skips symlinked directories, and is a no-op when `nltk_data` is absent. 10 tests.
